subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw persist a plain-text accessibility preference under `tui`, expose it only as a startup switch, or replace decorative TUI glyphs globally?
rationale: The accessibility need, current source paths, and dependency limitation are high-confidence, but the activation contract and canonical spoken fallback text are public product and config decisions.

options.title: Persist under `tui`
options.body: Add one documented terminal-only preference and a centralized rendering policy, including a proper pi-tui marker seam.

options.title: Use startup-only switch
options.body: Expose a CLI flag or environment variable while leaving persistent configuration unchanged.

options.title: Change defaults globally
options.body: Replace decorative glyphs for every TUI user and maintain a single rendering path.

recommendation.title: Persist under `tui`
recommendation.body: Add one documented terminal-only preference and a centralized rendering policy, including a proper pi-tui marker seam.

likelyOwner.reason: The TUI and centralized tool-display behavior originate in his feature commits, making him the strongest available owner for the public activation-contract decision.
